'''Andrew Herbert Eschenfelder''' (June 13, 1925 – November 1, 2024) was an American physicist.

== Life and career ==
Eschenfelder was born in [[Newark, New Jersey]], the son of Andrew Frank Eschenfelder and Grace Helen Griffin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://seabee.org/final-salute/mr-andrew-herbert-eschenfelder/|title=Mr. Andrew Herbert Eschenfelder|work=Seabee.org|access-date=November 6, 2026}}</ref> He was raised in [[Glen Ridge, New Jersey]], and he attended [[Glen Ridge High School]], graduating in 1943. After graduating, he enlisted in the [[United States Navy]], and was deployed to the [[Pacific Ocean|South Pacific]] during [[World War II]], which after his [[Military discharge#Honorable discharge|honorable discharge]] in 1946, he attended [[Rutgers University]], earning his [[Bachelor of Science|BS degree]] in 1949 and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in [[physics]] in 1952.<ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://oralhistory.rutgers.edu/explore/alphabetical-index/interviewees/1552-eschenfelder-andrew|title=Eschenfelder, Andrew|work=[[Rutgers University]]|access-date=November 6, 2026}}</ref>

Eschenfelder worked at [[IBM]] from 1952 to 1981.<ref name="a" /> During his time at IBM, in 1962, he was named a [[List of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=Eschenfelder&af=true|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=November 6, 2026}}</ref> and he served as president of California Institute of Medical Research in [[San Jose, California]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telegram.com/obituaries/pneo1035516|title=Andrew Herbert Eschenfelder, PhD|work=[[Telegram & Gazette]]|date=December 28, 2024|access-date=November 6, 2026}}</ref>

== Death ==
Eschenfelder died from complications of [[multiple myeloma]] in [[Saratoga, California]] on November 1, 2024, at the age of 99.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/obituaries/andrew-herbert-eschenfelder-saratoga-ca/|title=Andrew Herbert Eschenfelder|work=[[The Mercury News]]|date=November 24, 2024|access-date=November 6, 2026}}</ref>
